alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued September 22 at 9:44AM MDT until September 25 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, San Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The ground remains saturated from recent heavy rainfall over the
past week. After a brief break, deep moisture is expected to
return to southwest Colorado Tuesday with a few inches of
rainfall possible during the Wednesday through Thursday
timeframe. In addition, multiple rounds of showers and
thunderstorms are expected Wednesday through Thursday evening
producing periods of heavy rainfall and potential flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

afd.snippet: 000 FXUS65 KGJT 221948 AFDGJT Area Forecast Discussion National Weather Service Grand Junction CO 148 PM MDT Tue Sep 22 2026 .KEY MESSAGES... - Wetter weather returns to the region today, with showers and storms possible each day through the end of the work week. - There is a potential for moderate and heavy rainfall that could lead to flooding mainly in the southern San Juans and surrounding vall

fwf.snippet: .DISCUSSION...Moisture returns today with increased chances for showers and thunderstorms. The best chances for wetting rains will be over the central and southern Colorado mountains, but any higher terrain will see the possibility for a shower or thunderstorm. Precip chances and increased relative humidity continues through week keeping critical fire weather conditions at a minimum. ...GUSTY ERRA

alerts.title: US 160 Pagosa Springs Reconstruction-147574
alerts.description: Between US 84 and Pike Drive (Pagosa Springs) from Mile Point 144.3 to Mile Point 141.8. Road construction. Starting Thursday at 7:00AM MDT until Thursday, at about 6:00PM MDT. Full schedule below: • September 24, 7:00AM - September 24, 6:00PM Comment: Harman Park & Piedra Road-Work is underway at this intersection of US 160. Working hours will be intermittent day and night so motorists should plan for potential delays, Monday-Saturday. Please allow extra time to get through the work zone. Safety benefits of this work includes pedestrian safety upgrades and ADA accessibility improvements. Expect lane shifts and up to 15-minute delays. Crews will switch two-way traffic into the eastbound lanes, perform temporary striping operations and begin asphalt milling in the westbound lanes. Parking will not be permitted on US 160 and vehicles will be towed at the owner's expense. Westbound lane closures, 10’ width and 75’ length restrictions will remain in place 24/7 through end of 2026. Work is weather-dependent. For questions contact the project team at 970-335-9230 or Pagosa160reconstruction@gmail.com Project Webpage: www.codot.gov/projects/us160pagosasprings
